1	# Setting up JusPrin 2's host on a server
2	
3	JusPrin 2 signs in on a host of its own, such as `jusprinv2-stg.obico.io` on
4	staging. Accounts made through that host belong to the `jusprinv2` syndicate,
5	apart from any Obico account with the same email: the request's host picks the
6	syndicate (`obico-server/backend/lib/syndicate.py`). Google sign-in on that host
7	uses JusPrin's own Google client, so Google's sign-in screens are JusPrin's,
8	not Obico's. Each server needs this set up once, by hand.
9	`web_ent/jusprin/v2/tests/jusprin_host.py` builds the same rows for the tests.
10	
11	Staging was set up on 2026-11-10. Production has no JusPrin 2 host yet; its
12	host will be `jusprinv2.obico.io`, which the Google client already accepts as
13	a redirect address.
14	
15	## 1. The syndicate and the site
16	
17	The Django admin doesn't edit syndicates, so run this in a Django shell on the
18	web pod (`python manage.py shell`), with the host's name:
19	
20	```python
21	from django.contrib.sites.models import Site
22	from app.models import SiteSyndicate, Syndicate
23	
24	domain = 'jusprinv2.obico.io'
25	syndicate, _ = Syndicate.objects.get_or_create(name='jusprinv2')
26	site, _ = Site.objects.get_or_create(domain=domain, defaults={'name': 'JusPrin'})
27	SiteSyndicate.objects.update_or_create(site=site, defaults={'syndicate': syndicate})
28	```
29	
30	It changes nothing when run again.
31	
32	## 2. Google sign-in
33	
34	The Google client is "JusPrin 2 server", a Web application client in the
35	Google Cloud project `jusprin`:
36	
37	- Client ID: `477983024689-h769gibj38tbs3smov9mci575t0khkbf.apps.googleusercontent.com`
38	- Redirect addresses: `https://jusprinv2-stg.obico.io/accounts/google/login/callback/`
39	  and `https://jusprinv2.obico.io/accounts/google/login/callback/`
40	
41	In the admin, under Social applications, add one:
42	
43	- Provider: Google
44	- Name: `JusPrin Google`
45	- Client id: the client ID above
46	- Secret key: the client's secret. Google shows a secret only when it is made,
47	  so take it from wherever it was stored then, or add a new secret on the

## 3. Chargebee

JusPrin 2 sells credit packs and plans on a Chargebee site of its own,
`jusprinv2`, not on Obico's. Its test site is `jusprinv2-test`, which local
servers and staging use. Both sites use Chargebee's Product Catalog 2.0
(`web_ent/jusprin/ledger/billing.py` says what that changes).

Set these on the web pods:

- `JUSPRIN_V2_CHARGEBEE_SITE`: `jusprinv2-test` on staging, `jusprinv2` on
  production.
- `JUSPRIN_V2_CHARGEBEE_API_KEY`: a full-access API key of that site.

The site's product catalog needs these ids, which the server names in
`settings_ent.py`:

- Plan item prices `jusprin-hobby-monthly` ($10 a month) and
  `jusprin-workshop-monthly` ($20 a month).
- Charge item price `jusprin-credit-pack-USD` ($10), the credit pack.
- Coupon `jusprin2-obico-premium-20`, 20% off forever, for the two plans only.

Under Settings › Configure Chargebee › Checkout & Self-Serve Portal ›
Configuration:

- Checkout: turn off "Allow customers to edit quantity for plans", and turn on
  "Allow customers to add/remove coupons".
- Checkout: One time payments: leave it enabled; the credit pack is bought
  through it.
- Self-Serve Portal: set "Customers can access the self-serve portal" to
  "Via Single Sign On API". Otherwise Chargebee refuses the server's portal
  link with "Customer portal access via API is disabled".

Under Settings › Configure Chargebee › Webhooks, add
`https://<server>/ent/jusprin/v2/cb_webhook`, where `<server>` is the server's
own host (`app-stg.obico.io` on staging). The server trusts a post only for
the event's id and reads the event back from the site with its key, so the
webhook needs no password.

## 4. Check it

Open `https://<host>/accounts/google/login/?process=login`. It should redirect
to `accounts.google.com` with the client ID above and
`redirect_uri=https://<host>/accounts/google/login/callback/`.

Signed in on the host, open the prices page from JusPrin 2's Preferences and
start a credit-pack checkout. It should open a `jusprinv2` (or
`jusprinv2-test`) checkout page for $10. On the test site, pay with
Chargebee's test card 4111 1111 1111 1111; the account should gain 500
credits, plus the launch bonus while that offer runs.

input.recap: JusPrin 2 billing in tsd-enterprise now sells on JusPrin's own Chargebee site, and every path worked with the test card on jusprinv2-test. The change is uncommitted on branch jusprin-v2-own-chargebee-site and not pushed. Staging needs two env vars and a webhook before it can run this.

content.text:
JusPrin 2's billing in tsd-enterprise now uses JusPrin's own Chargebee site instead of Obico's. I tested every billing path end to end on the jusprinv2-test site with Chargebee's test card, and all of them worked. The change is in the worktree `/Users/kenneth/Projects/tsd-enterprise-worktrees/jusprin-v2-own-chargebee`, on branch `jusprin-v2-own-chargebee-site`, branched from master f9516b3f3e. Nothing is committed or pushed.

**What changed in the code:**
- Every Chargebee call in `web_ent/jusprin/ledger/billing.py` goes to the site named by two new environment variables, `JUSPRIN_V2_CHARGEBEE_SITE` and `JUSPRIN_V2_CHARGEBEE_API_KEY`.
- The calls use Chargebee's newer catalog API, which the new site requires. The credit pack is now a one-off charge, `jusprin-credit-pack-USD`.
- A new webhook at `/ent/jusprin/v2/cb_webhook` takes only the event's id from the post and reads the event back from Chargebee with the server's key. A forged post changes nothing.
- Obico's two webhooks no longer grant JusPrin 2 credits.

**Tests:**
- The 33 billing and account-deletion tests pass. On master's code, 21 of the same tests fail.
- The full jusprin and app_ent suites pass: 281 tests.

**Results on the real test site** (a local test account, checkouts paid with card 4111 1111 1111 1111):
- **Credit pack:** granted 500 credits plus the 500 launch bonus. Finishing the same checkout again granted nothing more.
- **Hobby plan:** granted 750 plus 750, once. The billing page's card line read "Visa ending 1111".
- **Switch to Workshop:** Chargebee changed the same subscription and charged $10 after crediting back the unused Hobby month. Hobby's credits ended, and Workshop's 1,000 plus 1,000 were granted once.
- **Cancel:** Chargebee marked the subscription "non_renewing", and the plan ends on 10 Dec.
- **Webhook:** I posted the ids of the 34 real events Chargebee recorded, each one twice. That rebuilt exactly the same credits as the checkouts did, with nothing granted twice. A made-up id got a 400.
- **Account deletion:** the delete endpoint returned 204, the local account was gone, and Chargebee showed the subscription cancelled at once.

**One setting I changed on the JusPrin test site:**
- The billing portal link first failed with "Customer portal access via API is disabled."
- I set "Customers can access the self-serve portal" to "Via Single Sign On API", which is how Obico's site is set. The link has worked since.

**Docs:** `docs/jusprin2-host-setup.md` has a new Chargebee section. It lists the two environment variables, the catalog ids, the checkout and portal settings, the webhook URL, and a check to run afterwards.

**Still open:**
- Before this reaches staging, the staging web pods need the two environment variables and the test site needs the webhook added. Without the variables, every checkout fails.
- Three known billing problems are not fixed here. The proposed fix for the first two is in `proposed-billing-fix.patch` in the notes folder:
  - A plan's credits are granted before its first invoice is paid.
  - Switching back from Workshop to Hobby in the same month leaves the Hobby credits expired.
  - After a cancel, the app still says "Renews" instead of "Ends", because `/v2/account` sends no end date.
- The test customer and its paid invoices are still on jusprinv2-test. I left them as test data.
- Branding, the sender address, Stripe or PayPal, the JusPrin 1 coupon codes, and activating the live site are still Kenneth's to do.

I added the full results to `chargebee-jusprin-emails-draft.md` in the shared notes folder.
Commit, no push

content.text:
I committed the port as 637f823933 on branch `jusprin-v2-own-chargebee-site` in the tsd-enterprise worktree. It is not pushed.

To your question: of the items I listed, two need a decision from you, three are things only you can do, and the rest I can do myself.

**Decision needed: fix the three billing problems before launch?**
- **Credits before payment:** say someone buys Hobby and their card is declined. The server grants the 1,500 credits anyway when Chargebee creates the subscription, so the person gets them without paying.
- **Switching back:** someone who moves from Workshop back to Hobby in the same month loses their Hobby credits.
- **"Renews" after a cancel:** after someone cancels, the app still shows "Renews 10 Dec." instead of "Ends 10 Dec."

You have two options:
- I fix all three on this branch now. The proposed patch was written for Obico's site, so I'd adapt it to the new one and test it the same way. That should take a few hours.
- You launch with them. The first one gives away credits whenever a card fails.

My pick is to fix them now. Do you want them fixed before this lands?

**Decision needed: which API key does staging use?**
When you approved the test-site key, you said it should stay in local dev only. Staging needs a key for the same test site. You have two options:
- Allow that same key on staging. It's one less thing to manage.
- I create a second test-site key just for staging. Then either one can be revoked without breaking the other.

My pick is a second key. Once you agree and decide when the branch lands, I'll set the two environment variables on staging and add the webhook on the test site. Which key should staging use?

**Things only you can do:**
- **Connect Stripe or PayPal** on the jusprinv2 site. This needs your own payment-account login. Until you do, only the test gateway works.
- **Activate the live jusprinv2 site.** Chargebee asks for business details and your own agreement to its terms. After that, I need your yes to create the live site's API key and add its webhook.
- **Verify the sender address.** Chargebee will email a verification link to jusprin-support@obico.io. I can trigger that email, but someone with access to that mailbox has to click the link. I haven't checked whether it forwards to k@obico.io.

**Things I can do without you:**
- Put JusPrin's logo and colour on the checkout and on emails, and adapt the email wording, on the test site.
- Find the JusPrin 1 subscriber coupons on Obico's site and create the same coupons on the jusprinv2 site. I'll show you the list before copying it to the live site.

**Nothing to do:** the test customer and its paid invoices on jusprinv2-test are harmless test data.

I don't understand any reason why we shouldn't fix those bugs. I didn't create those bugs. If you're not sure, ask the sessions who created those bugs, and if they couldn't justify them, fix them, right? Why did you ask me these?

You're right. Those are bugs in billing code that grants credits, nobody has given a reason to keep them, and fixing them is my job. I shouldn't have asked you. I'll save that lesson, then reproduce and fix all three.

"""What JusPrin 2 sells through Chargebee, and the credits each sale grants.

JusPrin 2 sells on a Chargebee site of its own (JUSPRIN_V2_CHARGEBEE_SITE),
apart from Obico's (CHARGEBEE_SITE), so its checkout, emails and invoices are
JusPrin's. Every call here passes that site; the module never uses the site
chargebee.configure() set for Obico. The site is on Chargebee's Product Catalog
2.0, so a plan or the pack is an item price and is bought with the *_for_items
calls.

The credit pack is a one-off charge (JUSPRIN_V2_PACK_PRICE_ID) bought on a
one-time checkout; its lot never expires. Hobby and Workshop are Chargebee
plans whose item price ids are JUSPRIN_V2_PLANS' keys; each term grants a lot
that expires with the term. Until JUSPRIN_V2_LAUNCH_OFFER_ENDS every lot comes with a
launch-bonus lot of the same size and expiry.

A lot is keyed by the invoice or the term that paid for it, so the checkout's
return and Chargebee's webhook can both report one sale and it counts once.

A JusPrin 2 account is a Chargebee customer of its own, jusprinv2-<user id>,
apart from any Obico account with the same email (lib/syndicate.py),
so the webhook finds the account by that id and never by email.
"""
from datetime import datetime, timezone as dt_timezone
from typing import Dict, Optional

import chargebee
from chargebee.environment import Environment
from django.conf import settings
from django.db import transaction
from django.utils import timezone

from app.models import User
from jusprin.models import JusPrinPlan
from .models import CreditGrant

CUSTOMER_PREFIX = 'jusprinv2-'
# Obico's own syndicate, the one an Obico Premium subscription is in.
OBICO_SYNDICATE = 'base'
SUBSCRIPTION_EVENTS = {
    'subscription_created', 'subscription_started', 'subscription_activated', 'subscription_changed',
    'subscription_cancellation_scheduled', 'subscription_cancelled', 'subscription_reactivated',
    'subscription_renewed', 'subscription_scheduled_cancellation_removed',
}
INVOICE_EVENTS = {'invoice_generated', 'payment_succeeded'}
# A plan in these states pays for its current term.
LIVE_STATUSES = {'active', 'non_renewing', 'in_trial'}


def end_plan_now(plan: JusPrinPlan) -> None:
    """Ends the plan now rather than at the end of its term, for a deleted
    account. A subscription Chargebee no longer has has nothing left to end."""
    try:
        status = chargebee.Subscription.retrieve(plan.external_id, env=_site()).subscription.status
    except chargebee.InvalidRequestError as e:
        if getattr(e, 'api_error_code', None) != 'resource_not_found':
            raise
        return
    if status != 'cancelled':
        chargebee.Subscription.cancel_for_items(plan.external_id, {'end_of_term': False}, env=_site())


def cancel_plan(user) -> None:
    """Stops the plan at the end of the term already paid for."""
    plan = JusPrinPlan.objects.get(user=user)
    result = chargebee.Subscription.cancel_for_items(plan.external_id, {'end_of_term': True}, env=_site())
    record_subscription(user, result.subscription.values)


def _when(seconds) -> Optional[datetime]:
    return datetime.fromtimestamp(seconds, tz=dt_timezone.utc) if seconds else None


def _grant(user, kind: str, credits: int, source_ref: str, expires_at: Optional[datetime]) -> bool:
    """Grants a lot, and the launch bonus beside it while the launch is on.
    False when the lot was granted before."""
    lot = {'kind': kind, 'credits_granted': credits, 'credits_remaining': credits, 'expires_at': expires_at}
    with transaction.atomic():
        _, made = CreditGrant.objects.get_or_create(user=user, source_ref=source_ref, defaults=lot)
        if made and launch_on():
            CreditGrant.objects.create(user=user, source_ref=f'{source_ref}:bonus',
                                       **{**lot, 'kind': CreditGrant.LAUNCH_BONUS})
    return made


def record_subscription(user, sub: Dict) -> None:
    """Keeps the account's plan as Chargebee reports it, and grants the current
    term's credits once. A term of another plan on the same subscription (a
    switch) ends the earlier plan's lots: the days left on it come off the new
    plan's first payment."""
    plan, _ = JusPrinPlan.objects.get_or_create(user=user, defaults={
        'external_id': sub['id'], 'external_user_id': sub['customer_id'], 'plan_id': plan_price_id(sub)})
    plan.external_id = sub['id']
    plan.external_user_id = sub['customer_id']
    plan.plan_id = plan_price_id(sub)
    plan.current_term_start = _when(sub.get('current_term_start'))
    plan.current_term_end = _when(sub.get('current_term_end'))
    status = sub.get('status')
    if status == 'cancelled':
        plan.expired_at = _when(sub.get('cancelled_at')) or timezone.now()
    elif status == 'non_renewing':
        # Cancelled at the end of the term: it ends when the term does.
        plan.expired_at = plan.current_term_end
    elif status in LIVE_STATUSES:
        plan.expired_at = None
    plan.save()

    if status not in LIVE_STATUSES or not plan.current_term_start or not is_v2_plan(plan.plan_id):
        return
    term_ref = f"term:{sub['id']}:{plan.plan_id}:{sub['current_term_start']}"
    if _grant(user, CreditGrant.SUBSCRIPTION, settings.JUSPRIN_V2_PLANS[plan.plan_id]['credits'], term_ref,
              plan.current_term_end):
        now = timezone.now()
        (CreditGrant.objects.filter(user=user, source_ref__startswith=f"term:{sub['id']}:", expires_at__gt=now)
         .exclude(source_ref__startswith=term_ref).update(expires_at=now))


def _pack_count(invoice: Dict) -> int:
    return sum(int(line.get('quantity') or 0) for line in invoice.get('line_items') or []
               if line.get('entity_type') == 'charge_item_price'
               and line.get('entity_id') == settings.JUSPRIN_V2_PACK_PRICE_ID)


def record_pack_invoice(user, invoice: Dict) -> int:
    """Grants the credit packs a paid invoice bought; the credits granted now,
    0 when they were granted before or the invoice isn't paid."""
    packs = _pack_count(invoice)
    if not packs or invoice.get('status') != 'paid':
        return 0
    credits = packs * settings.JUSPRIN_V2_PACK['credits']
    return credits if _grant(user, CreditGrant.PACK, credits, f"invoice:{invoice['id']}", None) else 0


def finish_checkout(user, hosted_page_id: str) -> Optional[Dict]:
    """Records what a finished checkout bought, when Chargebee sent the person
    back. What was bought ('pack' and the credits, or 'plan' and its id), or
    None for a checkout that didn't succeed or isn't this account's."""
    page = chargebee.HostedPage.retrieve(hosted_page_id, env=_site()).hosted_page
    if page.state != 'succeeded':
        return None
    content = page.content
    subscription = getattr(content, 'subscription', None)
    if subscription is not None and is_v2_plan(plan_price_id(subscription.values)):
        if subscription.customer_id != customer_id(user):
            return None
        record_subscription(user, subscription.values)
        return {'kind': 'plan', 'plan_id': plan_price_id(subscription.values)}
    invoice = getattr(content, 'invoice', None)
    if invoice is not None and _pack_count(invoice.values):
        if invoice.customer_id != customer_id(user):
            return None
        record_pack_invoice(user, invoice.values)
        return {'kind': 'pack', 'credits': _pack_count(invoice.values) * settings.JUSPRIN_V2_PACK['credits']}
    return None


def retrieve_event(event_id: str) -> Optional[Dict]:
    """The webhook event with this id as JusPrin 2's site has it, or None when
    the site has no such event."""
    try:
        return chargebee.Event.retrieve(event_id, env=_site()).event.values
    except chargebee.InvalidRequestError as e:
        if getattr(e, 'api_error_code', None) != 'resource_not_found':
            raise
        return None


def handle_event(cb_event: Dict) -> None:
    """A webhook event from JusPrin 2's site; one about anything but a JusPrin 2
    plan or credit pack changes nothing."""
    content = cb_event.get('content') or {}
    event_type = cb_event.get('event_type')
    if event_type in SUBSCRIPTION_EVENTS:
        sub = content.get('subscription') or {}
        user = user_for_customer(sub.get('customer_id'))
        if user is not None and is_v2_plan(plan_price_id(sub)):
            record_subscription(user, sub)
    elif event_type in INVOICE_EVENTS:
        invoice = content.get('invoice') or {}
        user = user_for_customer(invoice.get('customer_id'))
        if user is not None and not invoice.get('subscription_id'):
            record_pack_invoice(user, invoice)

"""JusPrin 2's billing: what a Chargebee sale grants, the webhook, chat titles,
and the pages the app shows in its sheet. Chargebee is replaced by mocks."""
import json
import uuid
from datetime import datetime, timedelta, timezone as dt_timezone
from types import SimpleNamespace
from unittest import mock


import chargebee
from django.contrib.sites.models import Site
from django.test import Client, TestCase, override_settings
from django.utils import timezone

from app.models import Syndicate, User, SiteSyndicate
from jusprin.ledger import billing
from jusprin.ledger.account import account, remember_chat_title
from jusprin.ledger.ledger import ensure_lots
from jusprin.ledger.models import ChatTitle, CreditCharge, CreditGrant
from jusprin.models import JusPrinPlan

TERM_START = int(datetime(2026, 11, 1, tzinfo=dt_timezone.utc).timestamp())
TERM_END = int(datetime(2026, 12, 1, tzinfo=dt_timezone.utc).timestamp())
LAUNCH_OVER = override_settings(JUSPRIN_V2_LAUNCH_OFFER_ENDS=datetime(2020, 1, 1, tzinfo=dt_timezone.utc))
LAUNCH_ON = override_settings(JUSPRIN_V2_LAUNCH_OFFER_ENDS=datetime(2999, 1, 1, tzinfo=dt_timezone.utc))


def sub(user, plan_id='jusprin-hobby-monthly', status='active', start=TERM_START, end=TERM_END, sub_id='sub-1'):
    return {'id': sub_id, 'customer_id': billing.customer_id(user), 'status': status,
            'subscription_items': [{'item_price_id': plan_id, 'item_type': 'plan', 'quantity': 1}],
            'current_term_start': start, 'current_term_end': end}


def pack_invoice(user, invoice_id='inv-1', status='paid', quantity=1):
    return {'id': invoice_id, 'customer_id': billing.customer_id(user), 'status': status,
            'line_items': [{'entity_type': 'charge_item_price', 'entity_id': 'jusprin-credit-pack-USD',
                            'quantity': quantity}]}


def event(event_type, **content):
    return {'id': 'ev-1', 'event_type': event_type, 'content': content}


class BillingTestCase(TestCase):
    def setUp(self):
        base, _ = Syndicate.objects.get_or_create(id=1, defaults={'name': 'base'})
        SiteSyndicate.objects.update_or_create(site=Site.objects.get_or_create(domain='testserver', defaults={'name': 'testserver'})[0], defaults={'syndicate': base})
        Site.objects.clear_cache()
        # The cached site would outlive this test's rolled-back rows.
        self.addCleanup(Site.objects.clear_cache)
        # An explicit id: base was made with one, so the id sequence may lag.
        jusprin, _ = Syndicate.objects.get_or_create(
            name='jusprinv2', defaults={'id': Syndicate.objects.order_by('-id').first().id + 1})
        self.user = User.objects.create(email=f'bill-{uuid.uuid4().hex[:8]}@example.com', syndicate=jusprin)
        ensure_lots(self.user.id)

    def lots(self, kind=None):
        lots = CreditGrant.objects.filter(user=self.user).exclude(kind__in=(CreditGrant.SIGNUP, CreditGrant.FREE))
        return sorted((lot.kind, lot.credits_granted) for lot in (lots.filter(kind=kind) if kind else lots))


@LAUNCH_OVER
class GrantTests(BillingTestCase):
    def test_a_term_grants_its_plans_credits_once_expiring_with_the_term(self):
        billing.record_subscription(self.user, sub(self.user))
        billing.record_subscription(self.user, sub(self.user))
        lot = CreditGrant.objects.get(user=self.user, kind=CreditGrant.SUBSCRIPTION)
        self.assertEqual((lot.credits_granted, lot.expires_at), (750, datetime(2026, 12, 1, tzinfo=dt_timezone.utc)))
        plan = JusPrinPlan.objects.get(user=self.user)
        self.assertEqual((plan.plan_id, plan.external_id, plan.expired_at), ('jusprin-hobby-monthly', 'sub-1', None))

    def test_a_renewal_grants_the_next_term(self):
        billing.record_subscription(self.user, sub(self.user))
        billing.record_subscription(self.user, sub(self.user, start=TERM_END, end=TERM_END + 30 * 86400))
        self.assertEqual(self.lots(), [('subscription', 750), ('subscription', 750)])

    def test_a_switch_ends_the_earlier_plans_credits(self):
        billing.record_subscription(self.user, sub(self.user))
        billing.record_subscription(self.user, sub(self.user, plan_id='jusprin-workshop-monthly'))
        live = CreditGrant.objects.filter(user=self.user, kind=CreditGrant.SUBSCRIPTION, expires_at__gt=timezone.now())
        self.assertEqual([lot.credits_granted for lot in live], [1000])

    def test_a_scheduled_cancel_ends_with_the_term_and_a_cancel_ends_now(self):
        billing.record_subscription(self.user, sub(self.user, status='non_renewing'))
        plan = JusPrinPlan.objects.get(user=self.user)
        self.assertEqual(plan.expired_at, datetime(2026, 12, 1, tzinfo=dt_timezone.utc))
        billing.record_subscription(self.user, sub(self.user, status='cancelled'))
        self.assertFalse(JusPrinPlan.objects.get(user=self.user).is_active)

    def test_a_paid_pack_invoice_grants_never_expiring_credits_once(self):
        self.assertEqual(billing.record_pack_invoice(self.user, pack_invoice(self.user, quantity=2)), 1000)
        self.assertEqual(billing.record_pack_invoice(self.user, pack_invoice(self.user, quantity=2)), 0)
        self.assertEqual(billing.record_pack_invoice(self.user, pack_invoice(self.user, 'inv-2', status='payment_due')), 0)
        lot = CreditGrant.objects.get(user=self.user, kind=CreditGrant.PACK)
        self.assertEqual((lot.credits_granted, lot.expires_at, lot.source_ref), (1000, None, 'invoice:inv-1'))

    @LAUNCH_ON
    def test_during_the_launch_every_lot_comes_doubled(self):
        billing.record_pack_invoice(self.user, pack_invoice(self.user))
        billing.record_subscription(self.user, sub(self.user))
        self.assertEqual(self.lots(), [('launch_bonus', 500), ('launch_bonus', 750), ('pack', 500), ('subscription', 750)])
        self.assertEqual(account(self.user)['credits']['total'], 500 + 2 * 500 + 2 * 750)

class WebhookTests(BillingTestCase):
    URL = '/ent/jusprin/v2/cb_webhook'

    def post(self, posted, kept):
        """Posts an event to the webhook, with JusPrin 2's site keeping the event
        `kept` under that id (None: it has no such event)."""
        if kept is None:
            retrieve = mock.patch('chargebee.Event.retrieve', side_effect=chargebee.InvalidRequestError(
                404, {'message': 'not found', 'type': 'invalid_request', 'api_error_code': 'resource_not_found',
                      'error_code': 'resource_not_found'}))
        else:
            retrieve = mock.patch('chargebee.Event.retrieve',
                                  return_value=SimpleNamespace(event=SimpleNamespace(values=kept)))
        with retrieve as retrieved:
            response = Client().post(self.URL, json.dumps(posted), content_type='application/json')
        return response, retrieved

    def test_a_plans_event_is_read_back_from_jusprins_site(self):
        renewed = event('subscription_renewed', subscription=sub(self.user))
        response, retrieved = self.post({'id': 'ev-1'}, renewed)
        self.assertEqual((response.status_code, self.lots()), (200, [('subscription', 750)]))
        self.assertEqual(retrieved.call_args.args, ('ev-1',))
        self.assertEqual(retrieved.call_args.kwargs['env'].site, 'jusprinv2-test')

    def test_a_forged_event_grants_nothing(self):
        forged = event('subscription_renewed', subscription=sub(self.user))
        response, _ = self.post(forged, None)
        self.assertEqual((response.status_code, self.lots()), (400, []))
        self.assertEqual(Client().post(self.URL, 'not json', content_type='application/json').status_code, 400)

    def test_a_pack_invoice_is_granted_once_when_paid(self):
        self.post({'id': 'ev-1'}, event('invoice_generated', invoice=pack_invoice(self.user, status='payment_due')))
        self.post({'id': 'ev-2'}, event('payment_succeeded', invoice=pack_invoice(self.user)))
        self.post({'id': 'ev-3'}, event('payment_succeeded', invoice=pack_invoice(self.user)))
        self.assertEqual(self.lots(), [('pack', 500)])

    def test_another_customers_event_changes_nothing(self):
        theirs = sub(self.user)
        theirs['customer_id'] = 'cb-someone-else'
        response, _ = self.post({'id': 'ev-1'}, event('subscription_created', subscription=theirs))
        self.assertEqual((response.status_code, self.lots(), JusPrinPlan.objects.count()), (200, [], 0))

All three are now fixed and committed, with nothing pushed. Before each change I made the bug happen on the jusprinv2-test site using real Chargebee events, then checked it again after the fix.

- **Credits before payment.** I started a Hobby subscription whose $10 invoice was unpaid and fed its three real events to the webhook. The old code granted 750 plus 750 credits; the fixed code grants nothing. Once the invoice is paid, the credits are granted.
- **Switching back.** On the old code, going from Hobby to Workshop and back to Hobby in the same month left the account on Hobby. Its Hobby credits were ended, while Workshop's 2,000 stayed live. Now the switch back restores the Hobby credits and ends Workshop's.

I fixed one more problem I found along the way. The webhook now reads the subscription's current state from Chargebee instead of the copy inside the event. Chargebee can deliver events late or twice, so an old "switched to Workshop" event could otherwise undo a later switch back.

Both payment methods now work on JusPrin's test Chargebee site. Your PayPal approval completed a $10 Hobby plan purchase. PayPal took the money, Chargebee started the subscription, and our server gave the test user the plan's credits.

**What I checked after you approved:**
- **In Chargebee:**
  - The Hobby subscription is active.
  - The $10.00 payment went through the test site's PayPal connection.
  - The buyer's PayPal account is saved as a valid payment method, with automatic charging on, so next month's renewal can charge it without the buyer.
- **On the local server:**
  - Recording the checkout gave the test user 750 Hobby credits plus the 750 double-credits launch bonus, both expiring 10 Dec.
  - With the 500 sign-up credits, the account shows 2,000.
  - The account reply says the plan renews on 10 Dec.
- **Stripe:** a card checkout through Stripe passed earlier.

The PayPal error you hit had a simple cause. Chrome kept filling the sign-in page with the shop's own sandbox email, and PayPal won't let a shop pay itself. Using the buyer's email fixed it.

**What's left before real customers can pay on JusPrin's live Chargebee site:**
1. **You turn on the live site.** None of the test setup carries over; Chargebee says each payment method must be connected again on the live site.
2. **Connect Stripe and PayPal on the live site** to the same TSD Technology accounts. Card statements will read "OBICO/THE SPAGHETTI DE" unless you change the statement name in Stripe.
3. **PayPal recurring payments.** Chargebee warns that a PayPal setting called "Reference Transactions" must be on for monthly renewals to charge. The sandbox worked without me changing anything. I haven't checked the live TSD PayPal account. If Obico's live site already renews subscriptions through that account, it's probably on.
4. **The server's Chargebee webhook** must be added on the live site, the same way as on the test site.
5. **Staging**, when you want it there, needs its own test-site API key. You approved the current key for local development only.
6. **Still open from before:** the site's look and logo, verifying the address emails are sent from, and what happens to JusPrin 1 subscribers' coupons.

I've added the gateway setup and the PayPal sign-in trap to the shared notes file, chargebee-jusprin-emails-draft.md. Nothing is pushed, and I changed nothing in production.

content.text:
No to both. I haven't tested on staging at all, so we're not ready for production.

**What has been tested:** everything ran on my local server against JusPrin's test Chargebee site, including:
- a credit pack purchase,
- Hobby and Workshop plans paid by card through Stripe and by PayPal,
- plan switches, a payment that hadn't gone through yet, and a cancel.

**Why staging isn't ready:**
- The server code is committed only on a local tsd-enterprise branch (jusprin-v2-own-chargebee-site, two commits). It has never been pushed, so staging doesn't run it.
- The staging and production settings files I copied on 9 Nov have no JusPrin 2 Chargebee settings.
- You approved the test-site API key for local development only, so staging would need its own test-site key.
- The app change that shows "Ends 10 Dec." after a plan is cancelled is also committed locally only, on its own JusPrin branch.

**Putting it on staging would take five steps:**
1. Push the server branch to tsd-enterprise master and deploy staging.
2. You create a second API key on the test Chargebee site for staging.
3. Put that key and the site name into staging's settings.
4. Point the test site's webhook at staging, so Chargebee's payment notices reach the staging server.
5. Then I'd repeat the purchases there (pack, plan by card, plan by PayPal) and check the credits in the app connected to staging.

**Production needs everything above, plus:**
- You turn on JusPrin's live Chargebee site.
- Stripe and PayPal are connected again on the live site, to the same TSD accounts.
- Someone checks that PayPal's "Reference Transactions" setting is on for the live TSD PayPal account, or monthly renewals can't charge.
- The production server gets the live API key, and the live site gets its webhook.
- The items still open from before: the site's look and logo, verifying the address emails come from, and what happens to JusPrin 1 subscribers' coupons.
Yes, do staging

# Before you start: read the dev docs

Before doing any dev work in this project, read the root `README.md` and `obico-server/CONTRIBUTING.md`. They document the dev process that is NOT obvious from the code and that you are expected to follow, including:

- **Dependencies:** declare packages in `obico-server/backend/Pipfile` and regenerate `requirements.txt` with pipenv. Do NOT edit `requirements.txt` directly.
- **Pull requests:** open PRs against obico-server's `master` branch, not `release`.
- **i18n:** a UI change that adds or edits a `$t('...')` string is not complete until all frontend locale files (`obico-server/frontend/src/i18n/locales/`) are synced. See the README's "Frontend i18n" section.

# Error handling discipline

- Do not catch an error merely because it can be caught. Catch only when the code can recover, translate the error at an abstraction boundary, or add context that is essential for diagnosis. Logging alone is not recovery.
- Represent expected states with normal control flow, not exceptions.
- Never turn an invariant violation or an "impossible" state into success or a silent no-op. Fix the invalid transition at the layer that owns the decision and let unexpected failures propagate to Sentry.
- Avoid duplicating defensive checks across layers. Keep lower-level operations strict, with their preconditions enforced by the caller that owns the workflow.
- If concurrency makes an invalid state reachable, fix the ordering or synchronization instead of suppressing the resulting error.
- Suppress an error only when it is genuinely expected and safely recoverable; document the reason and cover it with a test. Never broadly swallow unexpected errors.
- Prefer removing the root cause over reducing the visibility of its symptoms. Tests should encode valid transitions and assert that invalid ones remain visible.

# Start backend and frontend dev servers

This project uses Docker Compose. The backend Django server runs inside the "web" Docker container. you can start the backend Django servers by running `docker compose up -d`

** Do not forget to prefix all python commands with `docker compose exec web xxx`.***

The frontend server runs on the host. Use this command to start a Vue dev server:

1. Load nvm first:

```
export NVM_DIR="$HOME/.nvm"
[ -s "$NVM_DIR/nvm.sh" ] && \. "$NVM_DIR/nvm.sh"  # This loads nvm
```

2. Now you can start Vue dev server:

`cd web_ent/frontend && nvm use && npm ci && VUE_CLI_CONTEXT=$(pwd) npm run serve`

**Important**: `VUE_CLI_CONTEXT=$(pwd)` is required because `package.json` is a symlink to `../../obico-server/frontend/package.json`. Without it, vue-cli-service can load the wrong `vue.config.js` and write `webpack-stats.json` to the wrong location.

The dev server supports hot module replacement, so you don't need to rebuild after changing Vue files - changes are automatically detected and reloaded in the browser.

For anything related to Docker that you are not sure, check docker-compose.yaml and docker-compose.override.yaml to understand. if you are still not sure, stop and ask me.

# Pager on terminal

I use less as the default pager for Git commands (like git log, git diff, etc.). When generating Git commands, please always include the appropriate option to disable the pager, such as:

This ensures the output goes directly to the terminal without invoking a pager like less.

# Git structure

The top-level Git repo `tsd-enterprise` includes the public, open-source `obico-server` repo as a Git submodule. The dependency is strictly one-way: `tsd-enterprise` depends on `obico-server`; `obico-server` must not depend on or have knowledge of `tsd-enterprise`.

`obico-server` must remain able to run on its own. Hobbyists use it to run self-hosted servers without access to `tsd-enterprise`, its code, configuration, secrets, or private infrastructure.

Before making any change in `obico-server`:

- Decide whether the change belongs in `obico-server` or `tsd-enterprise`. Put enterprise-specific behavior and integrations in `tsd-enterprise`. Add shared functionality or extension points to `obico-server` only when they belong in the standalone project and preserve the one-way dependency.
- Check whether the change could break standalone startup, configuration, or workflows used by self-hosted users. Do not introduce requirements for enterprise-only code, settings, services, or credentials.
- Test affected standalone behavior using `obico-server`'s own configuration and documented setup. Passing tests in the enterprise environment alone does not establish standalone compatibility. If standalone verification cannot be completed, explicitly report what remains unverified and why.

The gateway's two streaming paths, `/ent/jusprin/v2/messages` and
`/ent/jusprin/v2/responses`, go to the websocket service (daphne), not the web
service: they stream for minutes, and gunicorn's sync workers cannot stream
them. The rest of `/ent/jusprin/v2/`, including `/models`, stays on the web
service. Both deployments read the gateway's alias config from a ConfigMap
(`jusprin-v2-gateway-<env>.yaml`) and the upstream keys from a Secret of the
same name that is created with kubectl and is not in this repo; restart both
deployments after changing either.

The path rules exist on every staging and production app host
(`app-stg.*` to `tsdws-stg-svc`; `app.obico.io`, `app.thespaghettidetective.com`
and `app.kingroon.com` to `tsdws-prod-svc`). The gateway shipped in the normal
release `obi.4048` (2026-10-25), so `stg/update-version.sh` covers both
environments again.

**JusPrin's host: `jusprinv2.obico.io` (staging `jusprinv2-stg.obico.io`).**
Decided 2026-11-04; named `jusprinv2` to keep it apart from JusPrin v1. JusPrin 2 is a syndicate of its own (`jusprinv2`, with its own brand in `SYNDICATES`; the `jusprin` brand is v1's), with its own accounts,
and the server takes a request's syndicate from its host. The desktop app's
browser sign-in runs in the system browser, which cannot send the
`X-Obico-Syndicate` header, so only a host of its own keeps JusPrin sign-ins
apart from Obico's. A separate host also gets its own login cookie (the server
sets no cookie domain), so an Obico website session cannot authorize JusPrin.
Rolling it out, staging first:

1. DNS (Namecheap, obico.io): A records `jusprinv2-stg` and `jusprinv2` to the
   ingress's static IP, the one `app-stg.obico.io` and `app.obico.io` resolve
   to.
2. `kubectl apply -f tsd/gcp/jusprin-managed-cert.yaml`, then
   `kubectl apply -f tsd/gcp/neg-ingress.yaml` (the ingress names the
   certificate, so the certificate goes first). A certificate is issued once
   its name resolves to the ingress. Both hosts are in the files:
   `gke-managed-cert-jusprinv2-app` serves `jusprinv2.obico.io`, and its rule
   routes like `app.obico.io`'s.
3. On the server, first move the syndicate id sequence past the existing
   rows: base and kingroon were inserted with explicit ids, so on 2026-11-04
   staging's next id was 2 (kingroon's) and production's 1 (base's). In
   `python manage.py shell` on a web pod:
   `from django.core.management.color import no_style; from django.db import connection; from app.models import Syndicate; [connection.cursor().execute(s) for s in connection.ops.sequence_reset_sql(no_style(), [Syndicate])]`
   (done on staging 2026-11-04 and production 2026-11-10). Without it the
   next step fails and rolls back. Then:
   `run_django_mgmt_cmd.sh set_up_jusprinv2_syndicate jusprinv2-stg.obico.io --google-from app-stg.obico.io`
   (production: `jusprinv2.obico.io --google-from app.obico.io`). It makes the
   `jusprinv2` syndicate and the site for the host, takes the site out of the
   base syndicate that a new site joins automatically, and puts Obico's Google
   sign-in app on it. Safe to run again.
4. Google Cloud console, the OAuth client of that Google sign-in app: add
   `https://<host>/accounts/google/login/callback/` as a redirect URI.
5. The desktop app's default gateway (`ProviderProfile.hpp` in JusPrin, the
   "jusprin" row) is `https://jusprinv2.obico.io/ent/jusprin/v2/responses`. To
   test against staging, set `jusprin_server/base_url` to
   `https://jusprinv2-stg.obico.io` in the app's settings file.

JusPrin v1 users signed in with Obico accounts on `app.obico.io`. The v1 import
leaves that sign-in behind, they sign up again on JusPrin's host, and their
v1 subscriptions are moved to the new accounts by hand

JusPrin 2 sells credit packs and plans on a Chargebee site of its own,
`jusprinv2`, not on Obico's. Its test site is `jusprinv2-test`, which local
servers and staging use. Both sites use Chargebee's Product Catalog 2.0
(`web_ent/jusprin/ledger/billing.py` says what that changes).

Set these on the web pods:

- `JUSPRIN_V2_CHARGEBEE_SITE`: `jusprinv2-test` on staging, `jusprinv2` on
  production.
- `JUSPRIN_V2_CHARGEBEE_API_KEY`: a full-access API key of that site.

The site's product catalog needs these ids, which the server names in
`settings_ent.py`:

- Plan item prices `jusprin-hobby-monthly` ($10 a month) and
  `jusprin-workshop-monthly` ($20 a month).
- Charge item price `jusprin-credit-pack-USD` ($10), the credit pack.
- Coupon `jusprin2-obico-premium-20`, 20% off forever, for the two plans only.

Under Settings › Configure Chargebee › Checkout & Self-Serve Portal ›
Configuration:

- Checkout: turn off "Allow customers to edit quantity for plans", and turn on
  "Allow customers to add/remove coupons".
- Checkout: One time payments: leave it enabled; the credit pack is bought
  through it.
- Self-Serve Portal: set "Customers can access the self-serve portal" to
  "Via Single Sign On API". Otherwise Chargebee refuses the server's portal
  link with "Customer portal access via API is disabled".

Under Settings › Configure Chargebee › Webhooks, add
`https://<server>/ent/jusprin/v2/cb_webhook`, where `<server>` is the server's
own host (`app-stg.obico.io` on staging). The server trusts a post only for
the event's id and reads the event back from the site with its key, so the
webhook needs no password.

content.text:
The server changes are on tsd-enterprise master as commit 2d97f4b1c7. They're the Chargebee port and the three billing fixes. I moved them onto the current master first: another session had rewritten the Google sign-in commits my branch was built on. All 287 server tests pass on the result.

I also pushed a release commit, e1c059176f, to the release branch, so CircleCI is building the new server image now. The release reuses the last release's website bundles, because nothing in the website's frontend has changed since then.

**What I need from you:** a second API key on JusPrin's test Chargebee site, for staging only.
1. Open jusprinv2-test.chargebee.com → Settings → Configure Chargebee → API Keys and Webhooks → API Keys.
2. Add a **Full-Access** key and name it "staging".
3. Save it in a new file, `~/.config/jusprin/chargebee-jusprinv2-stg.env`, as one line: `CHARGEBEE_API_KEY=<the key>`

**What I'll do once the key is saved and the image is built:**
- Add the test site's name and that key to staging's web server settings in the ops repo (`tsd/stg/tsdweb-stg.yaml`). The key goes in written out, the same way Obico's test-site key is in that file today.
- Switch staging to the new image and deploy it.
- Add the test site's webhook, `https://app-stg.obico.io/ent/jusprin/v2/cb_webhook`. The test site has no webhooks yet.
- Buy a credit pack and a plan on jusprinv2-stg.obico.io, then check the credits in the app connected to staging.

**Two things you should know before production:**
- **Releasing master now breaks production checkout until production gets its settings.** Master now expects JusPrin's own Chargebee site. If anyone releases master to production before the live site's name and key are in production's settings, JusPrin 2's credit pack and plan checkouts there will fail. Nobody has bought anything through them on production yet.
- **The ops repo has an unpushed commit from another session.** It's 3f5e1b7, about keeping JusPrin 2 chats on staging and production. When I deploy staging, I'll compare the staging file against what's running before applying it, so I don't roll out that session's change by accident.

- Stripe cards: the account's short name, then "*", then Chargebee's text (Stripe's statement_descriptor_suffix), 22 characters in all. Expected to read something like "OBICO* JUSPRIN".

content.text:
Staging is done and passes. jusprinv2-stg.obico.io now sells JusPrin 2 credits and plans through JusPrin's own test Chargebee site. In Chrome, I bought a credit pack and a Hobby plan, checked the Premium discount, and cancelled the plan; all of it worked.

**What I tested on staging, each with a new test account:**
- **Credit pack, paid with Stripe's test card:** the page said "1,000 credits added" and the account showed 1,500. The checkout's return and Chargebee's webhook both reported the sale, and it counted once (500 plus a 500 launch bonus).
- **Hobby plan:** the page said "You're on Hobby", with 1,500 credits a month until 31 Jan, then 750. Billing and usage showed "Renews 10 Dec" and the Visa test card.
- **Obico Premium subscriber:** Credits and plans showed Hobby at $8 "With Obico Premium's 20% off", and Chargebee's cart applied the coupon for $8.00. I stopped there without paying.
- **Cancel:** the plan stopped renewing and stays until 10 Dec. The account reply sends no renewal date and an end date of 10 Dec, which the app's "Ends 10 Dec." line uses.
- **Errors:** Sentry shows no new errors since the deploy.

**A bug I found and fixed on the way.** Local development and staging share the test Chargebee site, and both named customers "jusprinv2-<user id>". User ids repeat across servers, so a staging account could have taken over a local test customer's saved card and subscription. A local test payment could also have added credits to an unrelated staging account. Staging now names its customers "jusprinv2-stg-<id>", and each server ignores the other's customers. Production and local development keep the old names.

The fix has a test that failed before the change and passes after. All 291 server tests pass. That run also replaced the earlier "287 pass", which I found had run on an incomplete copy of the code.

**Where things are:**
- **tsd-enterprise master (pushed):** three commits — the move to JusPrin's own Chargebee site (77fd19cadb), the billing fixes (2d97f4b1c7) and the customer-name fix (a72b271f7e). The release branch carries them as image obi.4104.
- **Staging:** all four deployments run obi.4104.
- **Ops repo:** the staging changes are committed locally as 1e6caf7 and not pushed. They sit on top of another session's unpushed commit, so pushing would send both.
- **Test site:** its webhook goes to app-stg.obico.io.
- **JusPrin app:** the "Ends 10 Dec." line is still only on the local branch claude/plan-ends-line.

**One harmless failure:** one webhook delivery failed once. Chargebee sent the event before its own lookup could return it, retried about 80 seconds later, and the retry succeeded.

**Production isn't ready.** It still runs obi.4098, the image from before this work. Releasing master to production before the following steps would break JusPrin 2's checkout there:
- You turn on JusPrin's live Chargebee site.
- Stripe and PayPal are connected to it, with PayPal's "Reference Transactions" setting checked.
- Production gets the live site's API key and its webhook.

The live site's look, its email sender and the JusPrin 1 coupons are also still open.

# JusPrin resources

This directory contains curated, production-facing JusPrin assets. Generated decks, PDFs, render trees, archives, inspection output, and design-tool working directories remain on `jusprin-v2-poc` and are indexed in `agent-docs/jusprin/poc-reference.md`.

- `branding/` contains the soft-serve mark in the gradient, ink and white.
- `ui/` contains the authoritative semantic product UI tokens, `design-tokens.json`, which the shell, the Agent page, and `tests/brand/` all read.
- `images/` contains the application icons the bundle and installer reference directly (`JusPrin.icns`, `JusPrin.ico`).
- `welcome/` contains the clip on the first-launch welcome screen, which Home's page bundles, and the credit its CC BY 2.0 photos require. The clip is a placeholder until a recording of the real app replaces it. It also holds Google's own "G" mark for the sign-in door's "Continue with Google" button, in Google's colours as its brand guidelines require; it is the one literal colour on the welcome.
- `startup/` contains the name animation in two versions, each light and dark: the nozzle prints the name one layer at a time and drops the dot on the i. The macOS splash plays `splash-name-*` over the lockup's name, in the box `component.splash.name*` in `ui/design-tokens.json`; it loops, starting as the name finishes, because the splash may be up for under a second. The About window plays `about-name-*` on every platform over the horizontal lockup's name, scaled down to the box `component.about.name*`; it prints once from an empty name and stops on the finished logo. `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Brand/splash_animation.py` draws it from the logo geometry; rerun it rather than editing the files.
- `overlay/images/` contains the splash, About and horizontal lockups, monochrome mark, wizard watermark, and window icon PNGs under OrcaSlicer's asset names; `Slic3r::var()` serves them in place of the stock files. They also cover `OrcaSlicer.svg` (message, release-note and update dialogs) and `OrcaSlicer-mac_256px.ico` (the Mac Dock icon while the app runs).

Every logo file (marks, lockups, overlays, app icons) is drawn by `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Brand/brand_logo.py` from one geometry: the cone, and the name in HarmonyOS Sans SC Bold cut into print layers. The output is flat paths with one linear gradient, so nanosvg renders it without masks or text elements. Change the logo there and rerun it; do not edit the generated files by hand, and do not stretch or recolor them.

The search turned up Chargebee's documented path for this. In the Chargebee dashboard, you go to Settings > Configure Chargebee > Checkout and Self-Serve Portal > Fields. Use the toggle button to enable or disable a field. The billing section has per-component toggles, so you can switch off individual parts of the address rather than the whole block. Turn the toggle buttons on or off to enable or disable granular components of the address.

Some caveats from the docs:

- **Gateway requirements:** If your payment gateway requires certain address fields, you can make them mandatory on Chargebee's hosted pages. One support article says you can set the address fields that are set as mandatory in the gateway to be mandatory in Chargebee.
- **Checkout created via API:** When a checkout is created through the API for an existing customer who already has a complete billing address, or when all mandatory billing fields are passed in the request, the billing address is treated as final and is not editable by the customer. Make sure your API call passes all mandatory billing fields if you want the address locked.
- **Country restrictions:** Country lists are set per section, under Fields > Billing > Address Fields > Country, with an edit icon to modify the list.
- **Shipping option:** The "Ship to my billing address" option is controlled separately under Fields > Shipping. Disable In checkout, show the option "Ship to my billing address", then publish.

Two sources (an older doc version and the current one) describe the navigation slightly differently, so check the menu labels in your own dashboard. I did not find a specific setting that marks the billing address itself as optional versus required beyond the toggles and gateway mandates above. Confirm that in the current docs or with Chargebee support.

content.text:
I restyled JusPrin's Chargebee test site (jusprinv2-test) in JusPrin's branding. I checked it on a fresh staging checkout for a $10 credit pack. The empty band above "Back to cart" is gone: it was the header slot for a site logo, and the site had no logo uploaded. I haven't touched the live JusPrin site or Obico's site.

**What changed on the test site**
- **Logo:** the JusPrin soft-serve logo now sits in that header band. I also uploaded the square mark as the icon and the server's favicon. Chargebee also puts the logo on emails and invoices; its email preview now shows it.
- **Checkout colors:** buttons and links are JusPrin purple (#3A2D64). The page and header use the lilac page background (#F6F2F7), and the cards stay white. Corners are rounded.
- **Brand color** for emails, invoices and the self-serve portal changed from Chargebee blue to #3A2D64.
- **Font:** Chargebee only offers generic choices (Sans Serif, Serif, Monospace), so the checkout can't use HarmonyOS Sans SC. It stays on Sans Serif.

On the restyled checkout, the cart page shows the logo, "Your cart", the pack at $10.00 and a purple "Proceed To Checkout" button. The next page shows the account details, billing address and payment choices, with a purple "Pay $10.00" button. I left that checkout unpaid.

**The billing address isn't needed today**
- **Tax:** this is the main reason a checkout asks for an address, and neither JusPrin's test site nor Obico's live site has tax set up. Chargebee's tax page on both shows only "Configure Tax", with nothing configured.
- **What Obico asks for:** Obico's live checkout asks for first and last name only, no billing address. The card form then asks for zip and country, which card networks use for fraud checks.
- **What JusPrin asks for:** JusPrin's test checkout asks for a full address, with street, city and state required. Our server never reads it.

I tried to switch JusPrin's test checkout to match Obico. The permission check refused it as an account settings change, so the address form is still there. The question below the recap asks whether to turn it off.

If JusPrin later has to charge sales tax or EU VAT on credits and plans, the address (or at least the country) would need to come back. That is a tax question for you, not a reason to keep the form now.

The live JusPrin site needs the same logo, colors and field settings before it takes payments. I'll only make those changes with your yes, as part of the production rollout.

Sources:
- [Chargebee: Configure fields and labels](https://chargebee.com/docs/billing/2.0/hosted-capabilities/configure-fullpage-fieldslabels)
- [Chargebee: Address requirements for your payment gateway](https://www.chargebee.com/docs/payments/2.0/kb/billing/how-do-i-enable-address-requirements-specific-to-my-payment-gateway-to-process-credit-card)

input.recap: JusPrin's test checkout no longer asks for a billing address: billing and shipping are off, and the card asks only an optional zip and country. A $10 staging purchase without them added 500 + 500 credits. The setup doc is updated on master in 52d1bd7974; the live site is untouched.

content.text:
The checkout on JusPrin's Chargebee test site (jusprinv2-test) now goes straight from Account Details to payment, with no billing address form. I also wrote the settings into the server's setup doc and pushed it to tsd-enterprise master as 52d1bd7974. That way the live JusPrin site gets set up the same way when it goes live.

**What I changed on the test site**
- **Billing section off.** With only the address turned off, a "Billing Address" box was left asking for first and last name, right under Account Details, which already shows the name. So I turned off the whole billing section.
- **Shipping section off.** It had been copying the billing settings. Obico's site has it off too.
- **Card fields.** The card form asks for zip and country, both marked optional, as on Obico's site. Card networks use them in fraud checks.

**Tested on staging**
- A fresh $10 credit-pack checkout showed Account Details, then the card and PayPal choices, and the purple "Pay $10.00" button.
- I paid with Stripe's test card and left zip and country empty. The test account got 500 credits plus the 500 launch bonus (invoice 16).

**Still open**
- **Live site:** it still needs all of this, plus the logo and colors from before. I'll only touch it with your yes.
- **Tax:** if JusPrin ever collects sales tax or VAT, the billing section has to come back, with at least the country. The setup doc says so.

We're not ready for production yet. The server code is ready, but JusPrin's Chargebee account still has only its test site. The site picker shows "jusprinv2 – TEST Site" and no live site. Until a live site exists with its catalog, payment gateways and webhook, production has nowhere to sell. I changed nothing during this check.

**What's ready**
- **Server code:** master holds the move to JusPrin's own Chargebee site, the billing fixes, the customer-name prefix and the setup doc. Staging ran it end to end: a credit pack, a Hobby plan, the Premium discount in the cart, a cancel, and a pack with no billing form. PayPal was tested on a local server.
- **What master adds over production:** six commits and no database migrations. Production runs image obi.4098, built from master commit 0a75568378.
- **Production matches the ops files.** The only differences are web-socket replicas scaled down on purpose and env lines in a different order.
- **Low risk to customers:** production has one JusPrin 2 account, yours (k@obico.io). Buying there already fails today: as of the 9 Nov check, the JusPrin 2 plans did not exist on Obico's live site. Deploying won't break anything that works now.
- **Sentry:** no errors in the billing code. The one hit on `/ent/cb_webhook/` is the old Obico email bug from August.

**What blocks the rollout**
1. **The live site.** You have to activate it; Chargebee will ask for business details. Then it needs everything the test site has:
   - the three prices and the Premium coupon;
   - Stripe connected to TSD's live account, and PayPal connected to TSD's live account. On PayPal, "Reference Transactions" has to be on, or renewals can't be charged.
   - the checkout settings (one-time payments on, plan quantity off, coupons on, portal by single sign-on) and the field settings;
   - the logo and colors;
   - the "JUSPRIN" statement name;
   - a business name and address for invoices (the test site has none);
   - the email sender.

   I can do all of that once the site exists and you say yes. You create the live API key, as you did for staging, and I add the webhook pointing at production.
2. **Deploy.** Build a release from master and add two settings to production's web pods: the live site name `jusprinv2` and its API key. The customer-name prefix stays at its default.
3. **Ops push.** Two ops commits aren't pushed. One is mine, for staging. The other is another session's chat-keeping change, which is already running in production. Pushing waits on you.

**Not blocking, but open**
- **Google sign-in on production:** sign-in on jusprinv2.obico.io still uses Obico's Google app, so Google's consent screen names Obico. Switching to JusPrin's Google app is a manual admin step, and you'd paste in the client secret. It can happen before or after the deploy.
- **Email sign-off:** the test site's emails are signed "Jusprin-support", with a lowercase p.
- **The app's plan line:** the change that makes the app say "Ends <day>" for a cancelled plan is only on branch `claude/plan-ends-line`, not on `jusprin-dev`. It should land before the app release.
- **Staging leftover:** staging test user 491 still points at a subscription I deleted from Obico's test site. It ends 10 Dec and only affects that test account.

input.ask: Which Chargebee plan should JusPrin's live site use?

content.text:
You activate it from the test site, signed in to Chargebee as the site's owner. On jusprinv2 the owner is **jusprin-support@obico.io**. The login I use, k@thespaghettidetective.com, is only an Admin there, and Chargebee doesn't show it the activation button. Activating starts a paid Chargebee subscription for this site, separate from Obico's, so it needs a card.

**Steps** (from Chargebee's activation guide; I couldn't see the screens myself)
1. Sign in to app.chargebee.com as jusprin-support@obico.io and open the jusprinv2 test site. Click **Select Plan**. Chargebee says the button is next to the test site in the site list, or at the top left above the menu, or on your profile at the bottom left.
2. Pick a plan. The Flow plan is the self-serve one, with a choice of **Pay as you go** or **Commit monthly**. Click **Activate now**.
3. Choose USD as the billing currency, then **Activate now**.
4. **Contact for Technical/Billing Issues:** enter the company name, then **Save and Proceed**. TSD's Stripe account is named "TSD Technology, LLC".
5. **Billing Information:** organization, phone and address. Obico's Chargebee profile uses 1790 Willow Lake Ln, San Jose CA 95131. Then **Save and Proceed**.
6. **Payment Information:** your card, then **Save and Proceed**.
7. **Summary:** agree to the terms and click **Pay & Get Started**. Your bank may ask for a 3-D Secure check.

Chargebee then opens the live site. The site switcher at the top left now offers both Test and Live.

**Decision needed: which plan variant.** Chargebee's fee is paid out of what JusPrin bills, and only you can pick how much to commit. The options, using third-party trackers' numbers (I couldn't open Chargebee's own pricing page, so check it on the plan screen):
- **Pay as you go:** 0.80% of each month's billing, with no monthly fee.
- **Commit monthly:** $99 a month plus 0.65%.

Commit only becomes cheaper once JusPrin bills more than about $66,000 a month. My pick is Pay as you go. The old free tier, which covered the first $250K, appears to be gone. Do you want Pay as you go? The question below the recap asks it too.

**After it's activated, four things only you can do:**
1. **Invite me:** on the live site, invite k@thespaghettidetective.com as Admin under Team Members. Each site keeps its own team, so the test-site invite doesn't carry over.
2. **Create a key:** under Settings › Configure Chargebee › API Keys and Events, add a full-access key. Save it to `~/.config/jusprin/chargebee-jusprinv2-live.env`, as you did for staging.
3. **Connect Stripe:** sign in to TSD's live Stripe account when the connect window asks.
4. **Connect PayPal:** sign in to TSD's live PayPal business account when it asks. Make sure "Reference Transactions" is turned on for that PayPal account, or plan renewals can't be charged; PayPal support turns it on if it's off.

Everything else I copy from the test site: the catalog, checkout and field settings, branding, statement name and emails. Then I add the production webhook, run one small real-card purchase, and deploy.

- [Chargebee: Go-live checklist](https://chargebee.com/docs/billing/2.0/implementing-chargebee/checklist)

Chargebee's docs point to two places to configure the descriptor, and the menu paths differ between the older and newer documentation.

- **Chargebee site (older docs and support article):** Navigate to Settings > Configure Chargebee > Payment Gateways > Add a Descriptor. The descriptor applies to every gateway in your Chargebee site.
- **Chargebee site (newer Payment Preferences docs):** Go to Payments > Payment Gateways, then click Manage Settings from the Payment Preferences block. The Stripe-specific setting there is an option to send the suffix for Apple Pay and Google Pay as well as cards (default off).
- **Stripe dashboard:** Stripe's own business name is set separately, under Account Settings > Public Information > Statement Descriptor.
- **Per-transaction override:** Chargebee's API accepts a statement_descriptor parameter, which will override the descriptor you have set on your Chargebee site.

Stripe's limits matter here. Chargebee's documentation says Stripe enforces a 22-character limit for card transaction descriptors, including the asterisk * and spaces. In Stripe's format, the part before the asterisk (*) is set directly in the merchant's Stripe dashboard. Chargebee's guide suggests sending only a short suffix, such as "PRIME", to avoid truncation.

description: "How to drive the real built JusPrin app for a screenshot-per-step UX walkthrough (2026-10-28): scratch copies, the empty local_machines loop with the fake printer, why background app_* tools fail on Orca dialogs, and where screenshots land."

On 2026-10-28 I walked six scenarios (open-and-print, fix-a-problem) through the real app with Opus 5.5 and published the critique at https://claude.ai/artifact/XyVvteGiKhiJ6apUx8rcmR (34 frames, scratch copy at scratchpad/ux/ of that session). Kenneth's steer: start from files people actually download (MakerWorld 3MFs carry a full Bambu profile: printer, print preset, filaments, colours, bed type, designer, licence), not from generated STLs. `~/Downloads` has Tape_4_3MF.3mf (A1 mini profile), find_my_hollow.3mf (P1S, 3 colours, 233 mm wide, too big for an A1 mini), arrow_headband.3mf (P1S), general_purpose_hook.STL (bare).

**Recipe that worked**
- `ditto` the built .app out of `build/arm64/src/RelWithDebInfo/` into the scratchpad before launching (another session's ninja can relink it underneath you); the bundle id is already unique (`io.jusprin.JusPrin`), no re-sign needed.
- `ditto` `~/Library/Application Support/JusPrin2` to a scratch `--datadir`; set `jusprin.fake_printer=true`, `presets.machine` to the saved "Bambu Lab A1 mini 2", write `jusprin/fake_printer.json`, delete `jusprin/mcp.json.lock`.
- **Clear `local_machines`.** Kenneth's conf carries a `local_machines` entry keyed by the empty string (old Moonraker experiment). With the fake Bambu agent on, `init_networking_callbacks`' connect callback calls `DeviceManager::set_selected_machine("")` in a loop ("same lan machine, dev_id =, disconnect and reconnect"), the main window disappears and the log grew 700 MB in two minutes. Clearing the map fixed it. The loop has no guard; see [[fake-bambu-printer-sim]] and [[harness-fake-printer-cleanup]].
- Background `app_*` tools cannot press OrcaSlicer's custom `Button`s (no AX action) and the hit test at the dialog's screen position reports "belongs to a different process". `request_full_control` + `computer_batch` works for everything, including the Agent web view and the macOS file chooser (`cmd+shift+g`, type the path, Return, Return). Re-front the app with `open_application` when another session's harness steals focus.
- Every `app_screenshot`/`computer_batch` screenshot is written as a JPEG under `~/.claude/projects/<project>/<session>/tool-results/mcp-computer-use-blob-*.jpg`; copy those for a report instead of fighting `screencapture`.
- The dev build (-O0) slices a 38 mm part in over a minute; wait 45–60 s before judging a slice.

**Why:** the first launch attempt looked like an app bug (blank window, title "Couldn't save") and cost ten minutes; the dialog-click refusals cost another ten.
**How to apply:** reuse this for any "walk through the app as a user" request; keep scenarios on downloaded files; write the critique per step as what the person knows / sees / finds confusing. Related: [[live-test-built-app-on-mac]], [[drive-app-with-posted-key-events]].

name: scratch-app-driving-traps
description: "Seven traps met driving a scratch copy of the built app without screen control (2026-11-04): in-place binary copy gets SIGKILL, Home drops bridge messages while hidden, header popups need a posted NSEvent, lldb std::string args, wx Wrap reuse."
metadata:
  node_type: memory
  type: reference
  originSessionId: dea8379c-b02c-43a2-a254-4c2259672439
  modified: 2026-11-04T18:59:38.548Z
---

Met while verifying print-host printer window fixes on the scratch `.app` (see [[live-test-built-app-on-mac]], [[open-file-in-app-without-screen-control]]).

- **Copy a new build into a `.app` with `rm` then `cp`.** `cp` over the existing signed binary keeps the inode; the kernel kills the launch at once (exit 137, nothing logged).
- **A launch from a plain Bash call dies when the call ends.** Start the app with `run_in_background: true` and `exec`.
- **Home ignores bridge messages while the main window shows a project.** A queued `launch_monitor` through `JUSPRIN_HOME_DEV_URL` is sent by the page and silently dropped; switch to Home first (`m_tabpanel->SetSelection(0)` via lldb).
- **Background `app_click` does not reach the header's popup menus** (they are not listed as windows). Post the click into the app's queue with lldb: `expr -l objc -- @import AppKit`, then `NSEvent mouseEventWithType:NSEventTypeLeftMouseDown/Up location:NSMakePoint(x, y-from-popup-bottom) ... windowNumber:[popup windowNumber]` and `[NSApp postEvent:atStart:NO]`. Render the popup with `cacheDisplayInRect:` on its contentView ([[capture-mac-popups-for-platform-diff]]).
- **lldb cannot build `std::string` args.** This libc++ uses the alternate short-string layout: a 24-byte char array with the text at offset 0 and its length in byte 23 (≤ 22 chars), passed as `*(std::string*)buf`.
- **wx `wxStaticText::Wrap()` (Orca's wx) skips a width it already wrapped at and keeps the first text it wrapped**, so SetLabel + Wrap on a reused label comes back unwrapped. Use a fresh label.
- **With the screen locked, an instrumented dev page stops polling** (WebKit throttles the hidden page's timers; `document.visibilityState` is "hidden"). Run JS in it through lldb instead: walk `[NSApp windows]` → subviews to the `WKWebView` (match its title or `URL`), then `[webview evaluateJavaScript:@"…" completionHandler:nil]`; the page can `fetch()` results to the dev server. A menu item without a shortcut: `[[item target] performSelector:[item action] withObject:item afterDelay:0.5]` from lldb, so the modal it opens runs after detach.
- **A locked screen slows the whole app 2-4×** (2026-11-05: the same first-launch OrcaSlicer import took 46 s unlocked at 15:48, 226 s locked at 19:22, same build and folder). Compare timings only between back-to-back runs under the same conditions, old and new builds side by side.

Every build of the fork (and /Applications/OrcaSlicer.app) shares bundle id `com.softfever3d.orca-slicer`. The desktop-control tools resolve an app by bundle id and bind to whichever instance comes first, so `app_list_windows` returns `[]` and filtered screenshots hide the window you actually launched.

**Working recipe (2026-09-05):** `ditto` the built .app into the scratchpad, `plutil -replace CFBundleIdentifier -string com.jusprin.worktree-test`, `codesign --force --deep -s -`, then `open -n <copy>.app --args <model>` and `request_access` for the new id. `app_screenshot`/`app_click` then work and include popup menus. A display-scope `left_click` on the header did NOT open the fork's PopupWindow menus, but a background `app_click` did; take the pixel-level `zoom` with the display tools afterwards (call `app_release` first). Display-scope `Escape` does not close those popups; a click elsewhere does.

The MCP discovery file `~/Library/Application Support/JusPrin2/jusprin/mcp.json` points at the newest instance's `http://127.0.0.1:<port>/mcp`; `tests/mcp/probe.py`'s `call()` can drive real tools (e.g. `workspace_inspect`, then `report_slice_review` with sessionId/plateId/sliceResultId) to put the header into the Check-print state without lldb. lldb `expr` cannot call inline accessors like `status_row()`.

**Why:** On 2026-09-01 a verification pass screenshotted the stock app instead of the build; on 2026-09-05 the tools bound to another session's main-repo build.

**How to apply:** Confirm the pid with `pgrep -fl OrcaSlicer.app/Contents/MacOS`; never kill an instance you did not launch. `osascript` System Events by unix id still works to set `frontmost`. See [[jusprin-shell-phase-1-design]] and [[orca-inherited-teardown-crash]].

**"On another Space" usually means "on the other monitor."** Cost about ten turns on
2026-09-09 and produced a wrong report to Kenneth. `app_list_windows` returns
`is_off_space: true` and clicks are refused with "this window is on another Space";
`app_bring_to_current_space` then fails with "the user's current Space is a full-screen
app." Both messages are about Spaces, so the natural read is that the user is sitting in
a full-screen app — but with *Displays have separate Spaces* on, a window merely sitting
on the second monitor produces exactly the same symptoms. Kenneth was not in full screen;
the harness had opened on the Acer.

Tell them apart before saying anything to the user: take a **display-scope** screenshot
(`app_release`, then `computer_batch` screenshot). Its header names the monitor it
captured and lists the others — if the window shows up there, it is a monitor problem,
not a Space problem, and the display-scope tools can drive it immediately. Never conclude
"the user is in a full-screen app" from the background tools' error text alone.

The same flag also flaps: a window can read `is_off_space: false` and click fine, then
read `true` a minute later. Clicks delivered while it is true report `ok ... unverified`
and silently do nothing. **A click that reports "unverified" and changes nothing is not

Reproduced live by Kenneth on 2026-11-10 against production: in the sheet, Chargebee's hosted checkout for the $10 credit pack, choosing PayPal and pressing the PayPal button shows Chargebee's overlay "Complete your payment in the open PayPal window, or close PayPal to continue paying another way", and the payment can't be finished in the app. Cause (from code, verify): `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Shell/ServerSheet.cpp` binds `wxEVT_WEBVIEW_NEWWINDOW` to `wxLaunchDefaultBrowser(event.GetURL())`, so PayPal's popup opens in the person's browser with no `window.opener` link back to the checkout page, and the checkout never hears that PayPal approved. The bundled wx (deps/build/arm64/.../include/wx/webview.h) has `wxWebViewWindowFeatures` and `wxEVT_WEBVIEW_NEWWINDOW_FEATURES`, so a popup can be hosted in a child web view that keeps the opener. Likely fix: for pop-ups the checkout opens (PayPal), host them in a small app-owned window with a child web view instead of the browser; keep plain links going to the browser. Check behaviour on macOS, Windows (WebView2) and Linux (WebKitGTK) per AGENTS.md cross-platform rule; read `agent-docs/jusprin/design-system.md` before any UI. Reproduce first (Bug Fix Policy): the staging Chargebee test site jusprinv2-test has no PayPal gateway, so reproduce against production with Kenneth, or connect PayPal sandbox to the test site if Kenneth agrees. Done = PayPal checkout completes inside the sheet on macOS, verified, with a PR to jusprin-dev.
input.background: JusPrin 2 sells credit packs and plans through Chargebee hosted checkout pages, shown inside the app's ServerSheet (a wxWebView sheet over the main window) which the server signs in through POST /ent/jusprin/v2/web_link. The live Chargebee site jusprinv2 went live on production 2026-11-10 with Stripe for cards and PayPal (TSD Technology LLC's account) for PayPal. The sheet's 'Open in browser' header button already opens the same page in the person's browser as a workaround. Separately, PayPal declined TSD's application to save PayPal payment methods, so PayPal plans (recurring) may not work regardless; one-time packs are the case to fix here.

input.recap: PayPal can't finish inside the app's Credits sheet: the app sends PayPal's pop-up to your browser, where it loses its link back to the checkout. Nothing was charged. A fix is proposed as its own task; the purchase can go ahead through the sheet's "Open in browser" button.
input.ask: Have you bought the credit pack after clicking "Open in browser"?

content.text:
PayPal can't finish inside the app, so this payment has to go through your browser. Nothing was charged.

**Why PayPal is stuck:** Chargebee's checkout asks PayPal to open a small pop-up window. The app's Credits window sends every pop-up to your web browser instead, in `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Shell/ServerSheet.cpp`. That browser tab has no link back to the checkout inside the app. So even after you approve in PayPal, the checkout never hears about it and keeps showing "Complete your payment in the open PayPal window". You might find a stray PayPal tab in Chrome; you can close it. I've worked this out from the code, not from a separate test, but it matches what you saw.

**Finishing the purchase now:**
1. Click "close PayPal" on that overlay, or close the Credits window.
2. Open Credits and plans again and click **Open in browser** at the top right. It opens the same page in Chrome, already signed in.
3. Buy the **Credit pack** there. PayPal works in Chrome, and so does a card.

**Which way to pay:** PayPal is the more useful test. PayPal turned down TSD's application to save customers' PayPal accounts. A one-time $10 pack doesn't need that, so I expect it to work, but it hasn't been tried. Leave "Save this to your list of payment methods" unticked. Paying by card tests Stripe instead.

**Fixing the app:** I put the fix in a separate task, "PayPal checkout fails inside the app's Credits sheet". The app's web view component can host a pop-up in its own small window that keeps the link back to the checkout, which is what PayPal needs. It's a change to the JusPrin app and needs testing on all three systems, so it's better done apart from this deploy.
