Builds on [[live-host-check-via-instrumented-dev-page]]; used 2026-11-02 when screen control of the app was denied.

- Signed-in conf needs all of: `jusprin_agent.{provider=jusprin, jusprin_api_key, enabled=true, cloud_consent=true, jusprin_model_formats=<JSON id→format from GET /ent/jusprin/v2/models>}`, `jusprin_server.base_url`, `jusprin_onboarding.status=completed`. Without the formats the Agent says "not set up".
- An installed printer is `"models":[{"vendor":"Custom","model":"Generic Klipper Printer","nozzle_diameter":"0.4"}]`, not `vendors`.
- Kill the app before editing the conf. Replace a scratch binary with `rm` then `cp`: `cp` over a binary that has run gets the new process killed at launch.
- `Contents/Resources` in the build is a symlink to the worktree. Replace it with a real folder of links before corrupting a resource, or the worktree gets corrupted.
- Bringing the app forward triggers an account refresh, so to race the gateway (a real 402), change the ledger and send without refocusing.
- Page text input: native value setter plus an `input` event. A modal Preferences window's page polls as `agent-preferences`.
- A test preset needs a `version` field or import rejects it.
- A compose recreate drops env set by a wrapper; check `JUSPRIN_MODEL_ALIASES` before any chat so only the fake upstream is reachable.

Still needs the screen: pointer hover, native file dialogs, Orca's wizard.

The search didn't turn up anything about Chargebee specifically, and I found no source with the exact phrase "Save PayPal and Venmo payment methods." The results are about PayPal vaulting in general, and two of them describe failure patterns that could be relevant to your error.

- **Vaulting is what makes recurring billing work.** PayPal's Braintree docs say vaulting lets a merchant charge a PayPal account later without the customer present, and list subscriptions as a typical use. (Vaulted payments with PayPal account will allow you to charge the account in the future without requiring your customer to be present during the transaction)
- **Reference transactions must be enabled on the PayPal account.** Piano's integration notes that recurring PayPal payments depend on this, and that it's switched on automatically for successfully onboarded clients. (In order to run recurring transactions, reference transactions will be enabled by PayPal automatically on all successfully onboarded clients through Piano.) This is worth checking on your PayPal account if vaulting is refused.
- **Vaulting can fail even when the payment succeeds.** A WooCommerce support thread reports that vaulting runs as a separate step from the payment, so the payment can succeed while saving the method fails. (Vaulting works asynchronously with the actual payment and saving the payment method being two separate steps. The former can be successful with the latter failing.)
- **An "order not approved" error on a vaulted button** appeared in another WooCommerce thread, where the error showed up only when vaulting was enabled. The thread was closed without a clear fix. (This vaulted button UI is only observed when the Vaulting option is enabled)

For Chargebee specifically, you'd need to check its PayPal gateway documentation or contact its support, and PayPal's own support for the account's vaulting and reference transaction status.

I didn't find the dedicated Chargebee PayPal Commerce setup page, so these results are indirect. Recurring-payment setup is covered in pieces across several Chargebee pages.

- **Enabling Cards and Venmo:** Chargebee's release notes say you can turn these on yourself under Settings > Configure Chargebee > Payment Gateways, and that they use the same PayPal connection as PayPal wallet. The page is about 4,100 days old, so the steps may have changed. Chargebee no longer has to enable these methods for you.
- **Vault IDs:** Chargebee's Payment Parameters API doc lists the PayPal Commerce input formats. For Card, Venmo, and the vault-based PayPal Wallet, the reference ID is a PayPal Vault ID. The Billing Agreements wallet integration uses a billing agreement ID instead. The doc also says to use gateway_account_id to select the PayPal account. Use gateway_account_id to select the corresponding PayPal account.
- **PayPal wallet support:** Chargebee's wallet docs list PayPal via PayPal Commerce as the supported PayPal wallet option.
- **Reference transactions:** The PayPal Payflow Pro doc says reference transactions are required for recurring charges on that gateway. It also says Payflow Pro accepts cards only and points to PayPal Commerce for PayPal accounts. Although PayPal Payflow Pro supports accepting payments via PayPal, Chargebee only accepts payments via cards. To accept payments via your customers' PayPal accounts, configure PayPal Commerce. The Express Checkout doc says reference transactions must be enabled on the live PayPal account and aren't on by default in sandbox.

input.prompt: What does Chargebee say about recurring/subscription payments with PayPal Commerce: vaulting, reference transactions, billing agreements, any PayPal account approval needed, and what happens if vaulting isn't approved? Quote the relevant sentences.

result.output:
**Vaulting:** The Vault ID is created on a customer's first PayPal purchase and lets Chargebee charge renewals without customer action. As the page states, "The Vault ID allows Chargebee to charge your customers automatically without them having to perform any action" during renewals. "The Vault ID does not expire unless the customer cancels it."

**Reference transactions:** Chargebee requires them for live sites. "Enable reference transactions on your PayPal Business Account." "This is required for Chargebee live sites." "Reference Transactions are not supported in PayPal sandbox accounts."

**Billing agreements:** Chargebee doesn't use the legacy Billing Agreement ID for Cards or Venmo. "Billing Agreement ID (BAID) is the legacy token format and is deprecated by PayPal." For Cards and Venmo, "use Vault ID only."

**Account approval:** You need a PayPal Business Account, and Advanced Card Processing must be enabled. "A Personal Account cannot be used." Reference transactions must be enabled through PayPal Customer Support. Enabling Cards or Venmo also requires the right scopes: "Enabling a payment method fails if the connected PayPal account does not have the required scopes."

**If vaulting isn't approved:** The content doesn't say. It doesn't describe a vaulting approval step or what happens if vaulting is unavailable. For scope failures, it advises reconnecting your PayPal account from the gateway configuration page.

content.text:
**Ops repo.** There was nothing to squash or push. Someone, most likely the session coordinating server releases, already pushed all of it: GitHub's ops master is at bfad97a, the same commit as local master. My repo only looked behind because its `origin/master` reference was out of date. Squashing commits that are already on GitHub would mean force-pushing master, so I left them as they are.

**PayPal plans.** Today, someone who buys a JusPrin 2 plan with PayPal may hit a problem we haven't tested yet. Here is what I found.

- **Obico's live Chargebee site renews PayPal subscriptions every day.** Over the last 60 days it took 712 PayPal payments that went through and 52 that failed. In a sample of 60 recent successful ones, 59 were renewals. All the failures I looked at had code 10417, which means the buyer's PayPal declined the funding source. That is normal and not a setup problem. Obico's site uses PayPal's older connection type, Express Checkout, which stores a billing agreement for each customer and charges it at renewal.
- **JusPrin 2's live site uses PayPal's newer connection type, PayPal Commerce.** Its gateway page in Chargebee warns that without Reference Transactions on the PayPal account, automatic recurring payments can't be processed. Reference Transactions is PayPal's permission to charge a saved customer again later.
- **PayPal declined this for TSD.** When TSD applied to save customers' PayPal accounts, PayPal turned the application down.

My hypothesis, which I have not verified: the PayPal account behind Obico's site has the old permission for Express Checkout. Either it is a different PayPal account, or PayPal treats saving payment methods for the newer connection as a separate approval, the one it declined. If so, the first PayPal plan payment on JusPrin 2 might go through and the renewal a month later would fail. Or checkout might fail right away. I don't know which.

**What you can do to help.** Sign in to PayPal in Chrome. I left a tab open on PayPal's sign-in page; it signed out, and I can't type the password. Once you're in, I'll look up one of Obico's renewal payments (transaction 6HV94537A2906060M, $10.49 today) in TSD's account. That tells us whether both sites use the same PayPal account. Then I'll read the account's settings for Reference Transactions. All of this is read-only.

Decision needed: how do we find out for sure whether PayPal plans work on JusPrin 2? This one is yours because every option either costs money or needs you on the phone.
- **Call PayPal business support** and ask them to enable Reference Transactions and saved PayPal payment methods on merchant 5LEKESCBJJP9S, for use through Chargebee. This fixes the cause, but it may take days, and Chargebee says PayPal may want an authorized person on the call.
- **Buy the cheapest plan with your own PayPal on production**, then cancel it and refund yourself. This shows within minutes whether checkout works, but it can't show whether next month's renewal works.
- **Stop offering PayPal for plans** until PayPal approves, and keep it for credit packs, which don't renew. This needs a code change and a deploy.

My pick is the check after you sign in first, since it's free. Then the call to PayPal. Until PayPal says yes, I'd hide PayPal for plans.

**Other updates:**
- The session that fixed PayPal checkout inside the app's Credits sheet is finished. Its fix is commit 519189a293 on jusprin-dev, and it moved its test email to Trash.
- The scratch copy of the app that was signed in to production had already quit.
- Whether to turn on the other automatic emails on the live site is still your call.

Sources: [Chargebee: PayPal Commerce](https://www.chargebee.com/docs/payments/2.0/payment-gateways-and-configuration/paypal-commerce), [Chargebee: why Reference Transactions are needed](https://www.chargebee.com/docs/payments/2.0/kb/billing/why-do-i-need-reference-transactions), [Chargebee: PayPal Express Checkout](https://www.chargebee.com/docs/payments/2.0/payment-gateways-and-configuration/paypal_express_checkout).
